newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks wobble to weaker close, eye on RBA.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks wobble to weaker close, eye on RBA.

text.p: A choppy Australian share market wobbled to a weaker close on Thursday with rate cut expectations, a soft result from bank heavyweight National Australia Bank Ltd and July series options expiry all making up a less than clear picture.
The All Ordinaries index dropped seven points to 2,676.4.
"It was options expiry so I'm sure there was a bit of window dressing going on," said John O'Neill of Morgan Stockbroking.
"It is a bit hard to tell the true direction of the market with that coming into play. It's really been a bit of a flat day with everyone looking out for that rate cut," he added.

Reserve Bank action on rates was the broader focus of the financial markets, with weak wages data for the May quarter seen backing up the case for a near term rate cut made by Wednesday's key inflation data.
The only question in most trader's minds was when the local central bank would act.
"Some are seeing action as soon as tomorrow," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.

National Australia Bank's A$504 million (US$369 million) net profit for the June quarter put traders into a selling mood, generating active business in the heavyweight bank with a 60 cent trading range for the day before ending 2.3 percent or 45 cents lower at A$19.05.
The result was down sharply on expectations of about A$545 million, a portent of possible things to come, some brokers said.
"It looks like the first chink in the armour for the banking stocks that we've seen," said BNP Equities Head of Equities John Bowie Wilson.
Elsewhere in the leaders, mixed performances were the order of the day with no clear trend evident.
Among others, nickel hopeful Preston Resources rode higher, adding 51 cents to A$3.10 as traders took an upbeat view of its Marlborough lateritic nickel project in central Queensland.

Johnson's Well Mining NL, a member of mining entrepeneur Joseph Gutnick's stable, posted an impressive 94 cent gain to close at A$4.70 after Wednesday's announcement of a new gold find in Western Australia. However, brokers noted the very thin business with fewer than a dozen parcels traded.

The gold index took another beating, largely on the back of sector leader Normandy Mining shedding nearly four percent to close at A$1.47. Others to lose ground included Lihir Gold, down 3.8 percent to A$1.78 and Resolute, down nine percent to A$1.75.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about six to five, while 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
